analyst_view.overall: Córdoba (10th, 20 points, five unbeaten) host Real Oviedo (9th, 21 points), with both chasing the play-off places three points away. Córdoba come off a 3-3 at Mallorca after leading 3-1; Iván Ania says only the long-term injured and Diarra are out and Kevin Medina is back in training. Oviedo lost 1-2 to Girona in Raúl González's first game after Julián Calero was sacked; they have only 8 points at home but 13 away (fourth-best on the road), and against Girona most of their efforts were long-range shots. Pablo Sáenz (calf), Chris Ramos and Dani Calvo are out and in the numbers, Alberto Reina, who scored against Girona, is a doubt and Enzo Pérez is back from Spain Under-19 duty. The referee was still not named on LaLiga's match page on Saturday afternoon; both sides have been in high-scoring, high-shot form and the numbers already count that.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals, already adjusting for Oviedo's missing Sáenz, Calvo and Chris Ramos and both sides' strong recent scoring. Reina's doubt points slightly down for Oviedo while Córdoba's open games (3-3 at Mallorca) and Oviedo's good away form point the other way, so I stay at 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 11.5 corners and already add a lot for Córdoba's 48 corners in their last six. Ania says he does not know how Oviedo's new coach will set up away from home, so there is nothing firm to move on and I stay at 11.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.3 cards, already raised for both sides' recent card counts (23 and 21 in their last six). The referee was not yet named when I checked and I found no other new factor, so I stay at 6.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.9 shots, already raised well above a usual game for both teams' recent shooting (95 and 103 in their last six). Raúl González wants a pressing, direct side and against Girona Oviedo shot a lot from distance, but that gives no clear direction against the numbers, so I stay at 31.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.5 shots on target, already boosted for both sides' recent accuracy. Enzo Pérez's return helps Oviedo while Reina may miss out, which roughly cancels, so I stay at 10.5.
